raw_segments.text: I thanked her for her considerate choice, and as I really felt fatigued with my long
journey expressed my readiness to retire. She took her candle, and I followed her from
the room. First she went to see if the hall door was fastened. Having taken the key from
the lock, she led the way upstairs. The steps and banisters were of oak. The staircase window
was high and latticed. Both it and the long gallery into which the bedroom doors opened
looked as if they belonged to a church rather than a house.
A very chill and vault-like air pervaded the stairs and gallery, suggesting
cheerless ideas of space and solitude. And I was glad, when finally ushered into my chamber,
to find it of small dimensions and furnished in ordinary modern style.
